To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) a normalizing flow model is an excellent choice for modeling aleatoric uncertainty in a regression setting; (ii) the model’s performance is improved by using a calibration dataset to correct for model misspecification; and (iii) the performance is further improved by using a small recalibration dataset to correct for the model overfitting.

(1) the use of the normalizing flow is a promising method for estimating the uncertainty of a model, (2) the use of a normalizing flow is an efficient way to recalibrate a model, and (3) the use of normalizing flows can improve the calibration of a model in the presence of label noise.
